subject: Warm-pool occupancy scenarios, CMP routing, and egress safeguard
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan.park@helios-labs.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Naveen Rao <naveen@navisys.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask: private GPU pool for Helios - bursty ingest profile

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking this on. Quick context: Helios is moving a sensitive, low-latency feature set to a VPC private deployment. Traffic pattern is unusual — a sustained baseline of ~60 qps with 10–20% of requests being very long-context streams (10k tokens) and periodic bursts (5–10x) lasting 3–8 minutes tied to customer events.

Request: can you give us an occupancy projection and a recommended protection profile for burst absorption (warm pool sizing, scaling triggers, and an egress-safeguard approach)? We need a procurement-ready sizing brief to include with our purchase order by 2027-05-02. Key constraints:
- Max allowed egress per customer: 12 Gbps cumulative
- Preferred single-tenant warm-pool with fast warmup (sub-60s)
- Must support graceful degradation (priority routing to lower-cost quantized model)

I've attached Helios traffic sketch and our internal ingest curves. Let us know if you need simulated traces.

Attachments: occupancy-model-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Infrastructure, Helios Labs

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@helios-labs.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private GPU pool for Helios - bursty ingest profile

Evan — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers and next steps below; I put Jonas on CC for network folding validation.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Baseline 60 qps mean request size = 600 tokens; burst requests average 2k tokens but include ~15% 10k-token outliers.
- Target p95 latency goal during baseline: 120–180ms. During burst we accept p95 up to 750ms with graceful degradations.

Recommended capacity profile (first-pass):
- Warm-pool reservation: capacity to absorb 6x baseline concurrent concurrency (headroom = 6 * baseline). This translates to ~360 concurrent slots under our serving model.
- Burst lanes: reserve 2x of warm-pool as "burst slabs" backed by pre-warmed quantized model variants for fast spin-up.
- Scaling triggers: autoscale up when warm-pool occupancy > 75% sustained for 30s; scale down after occupancy < 40% for 120s.
- CMP routing (Capacity Multiplexing Policy): implement policy to route non-critical, high-token-length traffic to quantized lanes and redirect short/retryable traffic into cached-prefix lanes. CMP routing reduces cold-start egress by ~28% in our sims.
- Egress safeguard: enforce per-customer NIC policing plus a rolling window cap at the Redwood gateway (we recommend 10 Gbps soft cap + 12 Gbps hard cap). If soft cap hit, dynamically throttle long-context streams and fallback to 8-bit quantized model.

Telemetry / signals we need to validate sizing:
- Per-model active K/V cache hit rate (1s granularity)
- Warm-pool slot occupancy (per-lane)
- Per-tenant egress 1m/5m rolling sums
- Queue depth and per-request token count histogram

Attachments included: occupancy-model-v3.xlsx (first-pass numbers), network-folding-diagram.svg (draft). See sheet 'CMP-scenarios' — I used conservative 60% KV hit for baseline.

Next steps: Jonas can validate network folding (two-NIC split + egress fold rules). Marissa — can you prepare a short procurement stub summarizing committed warm-pool units and cost delta for burst slabs? Evan / Naveen — if you can confirm token distribution and any hard SLA minimums, we'll finalize the sizing doc by 2027-04-18.

—Stephanie
Senior Solutions Eng, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Evan Park <evan.park@helios-labs.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private GPU pool for Helios - procurement items

Looping procurement items as requested. Short summary for PO: 1) Reserved warm-pool units: 45 slots (equivalent to 360 concurrent slot-headroom as noted), 2) Burst slabs (pre-warmed quantized capacity): 90 slots reserved for guaranteed 5–10 minute bursts, 3) SLA tier: "Burst Guard" add-on with 12 Gbps hard egress cap and priority routing; 4) Pricing delta for dedicated burst slabs = +18% on monthly reserved fee.

I will draft a one-page billing annex and attach to the sizing brief. Karthik — please check the slot->GPU mapping and confirm per-GPU slot density assumption.

Attachments: sizing-notes.pdf (procurement stub)

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evan Park <evan.park@helios-labs.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: private GPU pool - technical note

Quick technical note to lock numbers before you finalize the PO: based on our runtime profiling (quantized LLM, mixed precision) and the requested headroom, mapping is: 1 A100-80GB equiv GPU ~= 8 warm-pool slots (baseline mixed workloads, KV cache present). For 45 slots reserved => 6 GPUs (rounded up to 8 to account for maintenance + fabric oversubscription).

Network folding (Jonas + infra): implement two-NIC egress folding:
- Primary NIC: steady-state RPCs and cached-prefix traffic (70% of baseline egress)
- Secondary NIC: burst-only slab egress, policed and shunted to quantized lanes when approaching soft cap.

Operational knobs:
- Batch size cap = 32 tokens for burst lanes; baseline lanes auto-batch 8–12 depending on inflight.
- KV warmup policy: keep last-10% hot prefixes pinned in warm pool for first 90s after cold start.
- Simulated headroom margin: plan for +25% headroom on top of computed concurrency to handle fat-tail 10k-token outliers and cross-tenant noise.

I'll drop a short mapping table into the occupancy-model-v3.xlsx and validate on ONPR-1284.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
